description: THE declared dependency set for a ClaudeFather install. Single source of truth read by cf-preflight (install time) and surfaced by Doctor (run time). Adding a dependency ANYWHERE in the framework means adding it HERE -- an undeclared dependency is how the appliance healer silently ran without `cryptography` for its whole life (see docs/CHANGELOG.md).

_tier_meaning.required: the install does not work without it -- cf-preflight exits nonzero
_tier_meaning.appliance: required only for the hardened appliance install (cf-appliance-install.sh)
_tier_meaning.optional: a named feature degrades or is unavailable; the install is otherwise fine
_tier_meaning.builtin_macos: ships with macOS -- listed for completeness + so a Linux port knows what it must replace

python._note: The engine is stdlib Python plus exactly ONE third-party package. Keep it that way -- a second one costs portability. CRITICAL: `cryptography` must be importable by EVERY interpreter listed in `interpreters` below, not just the one on your PATH. That per-interpreter split is a real failure mode, not a hypothetical.

packages.why: Load-bearing for FOUR systems: the credential vault (Fernet), Ed25519 superadmin grant verification, the signed-core update gate (verify_update.py), and the appliance healer's dist verification. Missing = vault DISABLED (every secret save fails) and the healer skips all updates + self-heal.
packages.gotcha: PEP-668: on recent Homebrew/Debian pythons `pip install --user` EXITS NONZERO without installing anything. Always verify by real import after installing, never trust the exit code.

interpreters.resolve: PATH python3 (or the ProgramArguments entry of the runtime launchd plist / tmux launch line)

interpreters.what: the interpreter the appliance runtime LaunchDaemon hardcodes, running as the non-admin runtime user
interpreters.gotcha: cfrun's home is /var/empty, so it CANNOT see any `pip install --user` packages installed by the admin account. Install system-wide for this exact interpreter, or ship a venv inside core.

interpreters.what: the interpreter cf-update-healer.sh uses, running as root via launchd
interpreters.gotcha: root has a different HOME than the admin who ran the install, so admin `--user` packages are invisible. Without cryptography the healer prints NOCRYPTO and `exit 0`s -- no update, no self-heal, silently, every 30 minutes.

binaries.why: the engine; every lifecycle script
every dashboard session, chief, and agent runs in a tmux session
binaries.gotcha: If the project lives on an external volume, tmux needs macOS Full Disk Access. `brew upgrade tmux` changes the binary signature and SILENTLY voids that grant -- consider `brew pin tmux`.

binaries.why: Claude Code CLI -- every chief, agent, Ralph loop and the Front Desk concierge shells out to it. Without it (or without auth) the dashboard boots green and every agent fails on first launch.
cloning + pulling the signed dist (updates and self-heal), cc-update.sh, the github storage mode, the pre-commit secret gate
every cc-*.sh / cf-*.sh lifecycle script
health checks, activation, mesh calls
cc-update.sh framework overlay, make-install-package.sh staging, cf-appliance-install.sh core copy
reads IOPlatformUUID for the LICENSE hardware fingerprint. No ioreg = no stable fingerprint = licensing falls back to hostname+arch, which is NOT clone-resistant.
macOS Keychain access -- vault_keychain key wrapping and Claude account switching
always-on supervision (runtime + healer LaunchDaemons)
macOS automation used by a few helpers
local TTS fallback provider for voice (when elevenlabs/openai are not configured)
power + thermal vitals
creating the non-admin cfrun runtime user
creating the cfrun runtime user with a service-range UID
ensuring cfrun is NOT in the admin group
the optional --immutable profile (schg on core)

`node --check` validates the ~10k lines of inline JS in server.py's PAGE string. Without it a syntax error can ship and kill the whole dashboard. Authoring-side mainly; harmless to omit on a customer box.
`tailscale serve` publishes the dashboard on the operator's own tailnet so it is reachable from a phone/laptop. NOT needed to use the box locally.
binaries.gotcha: The tailnet serve port MUST differ from the local server port -- the server binds 0.0.0.0 (which includes the tailnet IP), so the same number is EADDRINUSE and the server will not start. Convention: offset by +1000.

binaries.why: convenience for the github / icloud+github storage modes
reaching other machines in a multi-machine fleet (cc-fleet-ssh). Irrelevant for a single-box install.
make-install-package.sh builds the distributable zip. Authoring-side only.

_vendored_not_system._note: These are commonly MISTAKEN for system dependencies. They are vendored into the install and must NOT be added to `binaries` -- checking for them on the system produces false failures.
_vendored_not_system.gitleaks: vendored into bin/ by agents/security/tools/install_scanners.sh (best-effort, needs network)
_vendored_not_system.ffmpeg / ffprobe / yt-dlp: vendored under the media extension's STUDIO_BIN, not a system install

macos_permissions.needed_when: the project or data lives on an EXTERNAL volume (/Volumes/...). The internal disk never EPERMs.
macos_permissions.how: System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> Full Disk Access -> add the tmux binary
macos_permissions.gotcha: `brew upgrade tmux` changes the binary signature and silently voids the grant. Doctor detects the resulting EPERM. Do NOT restart the server to 'fix' it -- that re-attaches the same un-granted binary and hides the cause. `brew pin tmux` prevents it.

macos_permissions.needed_when: ONLY for the optional focus/context capture (reading frontmost window title + active browser URL)
macos_permissions.default: leave off for a first install; the feature degrades cleanly

macos_permissions.how: granted by the browser prompt on first use

macos_permissions.needed_when: NEVER for the web install -- the framework does not use osascript display notification or terminal-notifier. Notifications are in-dashboard. Only the optional desktop/native app would need a system grant.

power_posture._note: An explicit install-time CHOICE, not a default to stumble into. The two goals genuinely conflict.
power_posture.resilient: FileVault OFF + auto-login ON -- a power cut returns to a logged-in session so launchd/GUI agents restart unattended. Weaker at-rest protection for the vault ciphertext.
power_posture.secure: FileVault ON + vault_keychain:true -- protects the vault in a stolen-disk scenario; a power cut needs one human unlock before the box comes back.
